chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Abū ʿAbdillāh, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Jaʿfar, from his father, peace be upon them, who said:
"If Umm al-Walad kills her master by mistake, she is made to work toward paying her value."

Because we interpret this report to mean that when she kills him in a mistaken manner resembling intentional killing, then whoever kills in that way is liable for the blood-money if he is free, from his own wealth specifically. If he is a freed person with no master, he is made to work toward paying the blood-money, according to what the report indicates. As for pure mistake, its liability falls upon the master; and if he has no master, then it is upon the public treasury, according to what we have stated previously.

key_terms.أُمُّ الْوَلَدِ: a slave-concubine who has borne a child to her master
key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: financial compensation due for unlawful killing
key_terms.بَيْتِ الْمَالِ: the public treasury responsible for certain liabilities
key_terms.شَبِيهَ الْعَمْدِ: a form of killing that resembles intentional homicide in legal effect
key_terms.مَوْلًى: a legal patron/master responsible in this context

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if an Umm al-Walad kills her master by mistake in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This text presents a legal ruling concerning an Umm al-Walad who kills her master by mistake and explains how liability is assigned in different categories of homicide. It distinguishes between mistake resembling intentional killing and pure accidental killing, assigning the diyah either to the killer, the master, or Bayt al-Mal depending on the legal status involved.
